samples.summary: Keyboard-derived caret affinity never reaches the anchor round-trip, so the bug the editor.ts hunk claims to fix persists for Home/arrow-key carets
samples.evidence: `Cursor.moveTo` (cursor.ts:28-32) stores the affinity ONLY in `this.lineAffinity`; it never writes it onto `this.position`. Every keyboard path passes a bare position object: `this.cursor.moveTo(newPos, 'forward')` (text-editor.ts:2818, handleHome), `moveTo(newPos, focusAffinity)` (2780), `moveTo(newPos, isVertical ? this.cursor.lineAffinity : hAffinity)` (2795). The presence/anchor publisher reads the position object — `fireCursorMoveCallbacks(cursor.position, selRange)` (editor.ts:1160 and 2069) → `store.updateCursorPos(pos, sel)` (docs-view.tsx:399) → `anchorDocPosition(clampedPos, clampedPos.lineAffinity)` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2999). So `lineAffinity` is `undefined` for every caret that reached a wrap boundary via Home / ArrowRight / shift-arrow, and the new `restoreLocalCursor` code (editor.ts:3599-3608) falls back to `moveTo`'s `'backward'` default — the caret still re-collapses onto the previous visual line on the next remote change. Only mouse-derived carets (text-editor.ts:1521, where the affinity is put on `pos` itself) are actually fixed.

samples.summary: `cursor.position.lineAffinity` and `cursor.lineAffinity` become two independent, disagreeing records of the same state; a remote change can then make the caret jump a line
samples.evidence: `pos` now carries the click affinity (text-editor.ts:1521-1525) but several branches move the caret with the default: `this.cursor.moveTo(pos)` at line 1544 sets `cursor.lineAffinity = 'backward'` while `cursor.position.lineAffinity === 'forward'`. The painted caret uses `cursor.lineAffinity` (cursor.ts:48), while the value published to presence/anchors is `cursor.position` (editor.ts:1160). After the next remote edit, `restoreLocalCursor` re-applies the position's `'forward'` (editor.ts:3607), so the caret visibly moves to the next visual line with no user action. The same divergence exists for the cell paths (1591 `moveTo(cellPos)`) in the opposite direction.

samples.summary: Table-cell clicks and cell-internal drags never attach a lineAffinity, so the wrap-boundary bug remains inside table cells even though buildRects' cell branch now reads endpoint affinity
samples.evidence: Single-click inside a cell builds `cellPos: DocPosition = { blockId: resolved.blockId, offset: resolved.offset }` (text-editor.ts:1589) and sets `selection.setRange({ anchor: cellPos, focus: cellPos })` with no affinity; the cell drag path likewise rebuilds `pos = { blockId: resolved.blockId, offset: resolved.offset }` (1842-1845, 1861-1864, 1881-1884), discarding the affinity that was just assigned at 1795-1799. `resolveOffsetInCell` / `resolveOffsetInCellAtXY` return no affinity at all. So in wrapped table cells the highlight still opens on the previous visual line, which the cell branch of `buildRects` (selection.ts:268/365) can only fix if an affinity arrives.

samples.summary: The comment justifying `startAffinity ?? 'forward'` as "the historical reading" is wrong for the paragraph path, and the flipped default silently changes rect geometry for search highlights, spell underlines, comment markers and text-box selections
samples.evidence: Before this change the non-cell path called `positionToPagePixel`/`findPageForPosition` with no affinity, i.e. `'backward'` for BOTH endpoints (pagination.ts:385 default); only the cell branch hard-coded `'forward'` for the start. `const startAffinity = start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward'` (selection.ts:260) therefore changes behaviour for every caller that passes affinity-less ranges: peer selections from mixed-version peers (editor.ts:1620), search-match highlights (editor.ts:1640, 3129), comment markers (editor.ts:1659), spell-error rects (editor.ts:1676) and slides text-box selections (text-box-editor.ts:560). The change looks benign for a boundary start (the previous first rect was zero-width), but the in-code rationale misstates the prior behaviour, so a reviewer/maintainer cannot tell which consumers were considered.
searchedFor: grep computeSelectionRects call sites in packages/docs/src

samples.summary: Peer caret still resolves with hard-coded 'backward' while the peer's selection endpoints now honour affinity, so a peer's caret and the edge of their highlight can render on different visual lines
samples.evidence: `resolvePositionPixel(peer.position, 'backward', ...)` (editor.ts:1561-1565) ignores the `lineAffinity` now published in `activeCursorPos` (types/users.ts:27, yorkie-doc-store.ts:3004), while `computeSelectionRects(peer.selection, ...)` a few lines later (editor.ts:1620) reads `anchor.lineAffinity`/`focus.lineAffinity`. For a peer whose caret sits at a wrap boundary with 'forward' affinity, the drawn caret is at the end of line N while the highlight edge is at the start of line N+1.

samples.summary: handleEnd's shift focus gets no affinity while handleHome's does, so a reversed End-extended range reads the focus as 'forward' although the caret was moved 'backward'
samples.evidence: `handleHome` now sets `focus: { ...newPos, lineAffinity: 'forward' }` (text-editor.ts:2811-2814) matching `cursor.moveTo(newPos, 'forward')` (2818). `handleEnd` still does `this.selection.setRange({ anchor, focus: newPos })` (2827) with `cursor.moveTo(newPos)` i.e. 'backward' (2831). When that focus ends up as the range START (anchor later in the document), the new `?? 'forward'` default at selection.ts:260 reads it forward, contradicting the caret's backward affinity for the identical offset — the two are painted from different visual lines.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: Cursor.moveTo (cursor.ts:29-30) writes affinity only to the instance field, and every keyboard/typing call site passes a bare position object (text-editor.ts:2780, 2795, 2818 with newPos from getVisualLineStart at 4061-4064 and moveRight/moveLeft at 3887/3934, plus the getWrapAffinity insert paths at 322/548/733/3621/3676/3748). The presence publisher passes that same object unchanged (editor.ts:2069 and 1160 → fireCursorMoveCallbacks at 1185-1194), docs-view.tsx:399/407 forwards it to store.updateCursorPos, and yorkie-doc-store.ts:2999 anchors with clampedPos.lineAffinity — undefined for keyboard carets. Resolution only re-emits affinity when the anchor carried one (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1059, 1077, 1129), so restoreLocalCursor (editor.ts:3592-3608) omits both the spread and the 2nd arg and moveTo's 'backward' default wins. Nothing recomputes affinity afterwards (validateCursorPosition at editor.ts:960-968 only handles missing blocks; rendering reads cursor.lineAffinity at cursor.ts:41-52). Repo-wide greps for `ffinity` in packages/frontend/src and for withAffinity/position.lineAffinity found no alternate producer, so only pixel-derived carets (text-editor.ts:1517-1525, 1622/1625) and selection endpoints (2778, 2813) actually survive the round trip. The wrap-boundary caret restoration the new hunk claims to fix therefore still regresses for Home/arrow/shift-arrow carets on every remote change — a real incorrect-state bug on a live collaborative path, not documented as out of scope by docs/tasks/active/20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md:60-67.

finding.summary: clampPosToModel swallows an unresolvable blockId, but the very next call (anchorDocPosition) rethrows it uncaught from updateCursorPos
finding.evidence: clampPosToModel (l.957-977, touched by this delta) wraps everything in try/catch and returns `pos` unchanged when the block cannot be resolved — resolveBlockTreePath throws `Block not found: ${blockId}` (l.867). updateCursorPos then immediately calls `this.anchorDocPosition(clampedPos, clampedPos.lineAffinity)` (l.2999) with that same unresolvable position, and anchorDocPosition has no try/catch and no `if (!block)` guard: l.925 resolveBlockTreePath throws, or if it does resolve, `getBlockByRegion` (typed `Block` but can return `undefined` at runtime, l.1383-1394) feeds `this.blockTextLength(block)` at l.928 → TypeError. anchorDocRange (l.994) has the same exposure for selection endpoints. So the defensive catch added in clampPosToModel is illusory: a caret referencing a block a remote peer just deleted still throws out of updateCursorPos, which is called from the editor's cursor-move path with no caller-side handling.

verdict.reason: Every cited location checks out. clampPosToModel (yorkie-doc-store.ts:957-977) swallows the `Block not found` error thrown by resolveBlockTreePath (l.867) and returns the unresolvable `pos` unchanged, and also has an `if (!block) return pos` at l.962. updateCursorPos then passes that same position straight into anchorDocPosition at l.2999, which has no try/catch and no null guard: l.925 calls resolveBlockTreePath (throws) and l.928 dereferences `block.inlines` via blockTextLength on the result of getBlockByRegion, which is typed `: Block` but returns `blocks[topIndex]` with no existence check (l.1383-1394), so `undefined` is possible at runtime. anchorDocRange (l.994-1011) routes both selection endpoints through the same unguarded anchorDocPosition at l.999/1002. Callers do not handle it: docs-view.tsx:399 calls updateCursorPos inside editor.onCursorMove with no try/catch, and docs-view.tsx:405-409 re-invokes it from a window.setTimeout trailing callback using a `pos` captured up to CURSOR_UPDATE_THROTTLE ms earlier — a concrete race window for a remote peer to delete the referenced block, with the throw landing unhandled in a timer callback. setCursorForHistory (l.2883) is a further unguarded entry point. I found no guard anywhere that makes the unresolvable-block path unreachable; the author's own catch and !block check are themselves evidence the case is considered possible. This is an unguarded crash on a real path in the cursor-move flow, squarely in the correctness lane.
